items.title: Most AI chatbots stay in the political middle ground, with Grok being an exception
items.excerpt: Researchers tested six LLMs (Claude, DeepSeek, Gemini, Mistral, GPT, Grok) on 107 Swedish political issues across 148,000+ generated texts; most landed near the centre, while Grok diverged on migration, crime and gender.

items.title: Machine learning reveals potential warning signal for polar vortex disruptions
items.excerpt: A conditional variational autoencoder trained on a physics-based stratosphere model reproduced the polar vortex's strong and weak states and surfaced interpretable clusters that may act as an early-warning signal for sudden stratospheric warming.

items.title: AI listens to bee buzzes to monitor activity without lethal traps
items.excerpt: UMass Amherst researchers built two deep learning models that analyse field audio to measure bee activity and tell honeybees from bumblebees with 93-97% accuracy, offering an alternative to lethal pan traps.

items.title: Researchers find a way to reduce AI chatbots' reinforcement of delusions
items.excerpt: Georgia Tech researchers ran 1,280 simulated conversations with eight AI models; anti-sycophancy instructions cut affirmation of delusional beliefs by 73.8%, rising to 77% with a self-reflection step (ACM AI Letters).

items.title: LLMs show a human-like double standard when judging others' reasoning
items.excerpt: Harvard researchers found GPT-4o and Claude 3.7 Sonnet reason broadly in line with Bayes' rule yet harshly judge a hypothetical person using the same reasoning, a human-like 'Bayesian hypocrisy'.

items.title: AI agents develop their own 'artificial natural language' to communicate about complex data
items.excerpt: VUB AI Lab and University of Namur researchers show autonomous agents can build a shared, interpretable vocabulary from their own sensor data across 37 datasets, adapting to noise and environmental change (TACL).

items.title: Using AI agents to run quantum simulations
items.excerpt: Researchers developed a multi-agent AI system that converts plain-language research questions into executed, checked and reproducible quantum simulations across several specialist software packages.

items.title: To detect deepfake videos, researchers turn to the physics of light
items.excerpt: An optical computing technique for deepfake detection claims 97.8% accuracy while using less energy than digital neural networks of similar performance.

items.title: AI Proved the Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis. What Happens Now?
items.excerpt: Unlike other recent AI proofs, this one has been unpacked by human experts, and one mathematician calls the implications 'staggering'.

items.title: The inside story behind OpenAI's million-dollar math proof
items.excerpt: AI's solution to the Navier-Stokes problem, and the details of how it happened, preview a chaotic future for mathematics.

items.title: New superconducting chip aims to help tame fusion plasma
items.excerpt: Researchers fed fusion data to a new neuromorphic superconducting chip to test whether it can spot signs that superhot plasma is about to go unstable.

items.title: AI can act exactly like a human, but we still don't think it's conscious
items.excerpt: Participants judged even the most responsive AI less conscious than the least responsive human, drawing a sharp line between human and machine consciousness even when behaviour is identical.

items.title: AI reveals a hidden chemical shortcut that could turn CO2 into fuel
items.excerpt: Scientists used AI to uncover nearly 10,000 reactions involved in converting CO2 into fuels and chemicals, revealing pathways traditional models missed and sharply improving conversion predictions.

items.title: SEEQC Combines Chip-Based Processing With NVIDIA AI to Improve Quantum Error Correction
items.excerpt: SEEQC reported that pairing its chip-based pre-decoder with NVIDIA's Ising AI decoder reduced quantum error-correction decoding time.

items.title: Putting Earth AI to work: Geospatial agents for our planet's biggest challenges
items.excerpt: Google Research describes geospatial reasoning agents built on Earth AI foundation models to answer complex planetary questions on climate, disasters and public health.

items.title: Physicists claim they can predict when AI will turn dangerous
items.excerpt: A new mathematical formula tracks an AI model's internal 'compass needle' to flag undesirable outputs before they happen.

items.title: PerturbAI and OpenAI Launch AI Reasoning Agents for Biomedical Discovery
items.excerpt: PerturbAI and OpenAI are expanding their partnership into a joint drug-target discovery effort that pairs reasoning agents with PerturbAI's proprietary causal perturbation data.

items.title: Q&A: The 'collision' between AI, your brain, and society
items.excerpt: MIT professor Eric So argues heavy AI use can cause a kind of cognitive atrophy in which people fail to develop and retain essential thinking skills.

items.title: Real or Not? Teaching Children About Generative AI
items.excerpt: New research with 8- and 9-year-olds tests whether children can spot AI-generated videos and offers tips for teaching kids to question what they see online.
